rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is sparse, so this experiment tests a balanced multimodal (multimodal) and multiprofile configuration (config_019) using resnet50 (cost-effective) and pca_n2000 (dimensionality reduction) with avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion. This clarifies the effectiveness of combining both modalities for multiprofile tasks while keeping costs manageable. It is the best use of the first experiment to establish a baseline for multimodal performance.

The existing evidence shows that config_019 (multimodal multiprofile with pca_n2000 RNA, resnet50 image, avgpool, weighted fusion) achieves 0.638 accuracy. This experiment tests replacing resnet50 with the more powerful imagenet_vit_l image encoder and switching to transformer aggregation, which could better capture complex interactions in multimodal data. This balances exploration (testing stronger image features) and exploitation (building on previous multimodal success). The expected cost is higher than config_019 (estimated ~15 GPU hours) but justified by potential accuracy gains from advanced encoders and aggregation.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal, multiprofile configurations with pca_n2000 RNA and resnet50 image encoders (config_019) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.639). This experiment tests replacing the RNA encoder with scgpt (a more sophisticated model) while keeping other components (avgpool aggregation, weighted fusion) consistent. This clarifies whether RNA encoder choice significantly impacts performance. The expected cost is similar to config_019 (10.60 GPU hours), balancing exploration of a key design choice with cost efficiency.

The existing evidence shows config_019 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, weighted) achieves the highest accuracy (0.639) so far. This experiment tests replacing the RNA encoder with scvi_n200 (more advanced than pca_n2000) and the image encoder with imagenet_vit_l (more capable than resnet50), while retaining the high-performing avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion. This balances exploration of better encoders with leveraging proven components, and the expected cost (~8-10 GPU hours) is manageable within the budget.

Existing evidence shows config_048 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l) achieves the highest accuracy (0.7062) with moderate cost (4.82 GPU hours). This experiment tests whether swapping the image encoder to resnet50 (a simpler model) maintains similar performance while reducing cost. It clarifies the importance of the image encoder choice and offers a cheaper alternative if accuracy remains high, balancing exploration and cost efficiency.

Existing evidence shows config_048 (avgpool, weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.706). This experiment tests replacing avgpool with transformer aggregation while keeping the high-performing scvi_n200 RNA encoder and imagenet_vit_l image encoder. Transformer aggregation may capture more complex interactions, potentially improving accuracy. Expected cost is similar to previous transformer-based experiments (4.5-4.8 GPU hours). This balances exploitation of proven components with exploration of aggregation method improvements.

The existing evidence shows config_029 (multimodal, scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy (0.725). This experiment tests changing fusion from weighted to concat while keeping the transformer aggregation, which could reveal if alternative fusion methods improve performance. It's a logical extension of the current best configuration and has a similar expected cost (3.60 GPU hours), balancing exploitation of promising components with exploration of fusion variations.

Existing evidence shows that configurations using scvi_n200 RNA encoder and transformer aggregation (e.g., config_029) achieve high accuracy. This experiment tests whether using resnet50 image encoder (instead of imagenet_vit_l) maintains similar performance while reducing cost. It clarifies the importance of image encoder choice and balances exploration with cost efficiency, as resnet50 is cheaper than imagenet_vit_l. Expected cost: ~4.5 GPU hours.

Existing evidence shows that scvi_n200 with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (config_029) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.724989). This experiment tests scvi_n200 with resnet50 image encoder and concat fusion, which could clarify if changing the image encoder (to a cheaper alternative) and fusion method impacts accuracy. It is a logical extension of previous experiments with scvi_n200 and transformer aggregation, and the expected cost (around 4.5 GPU hours) is lower than config_029, balancing exploration and exploitation under the remaining budget.

Existing evidence shows that configurations using transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (e.g., config_029 with 0.725 accuracy) perform best. This experiment tests pca_n2000 RNA encoder with resnet50 image encoder, which balances cost and potential performance. It clarifies if transformer aggregation with pca_n2000 can match scvi_n200's effectiveness. Expected cost: ~12 GPU hours (similar to config_019's 10.60, but transformer aggregation adds complexity).
